 OilersNation has no direct affiliation to the Edmonton Oilers, Oilers Entertainment Group, NHL, or NHLPA Pre-Scout: Oilers start road trip vs. scary Schaefer and his Islanders Photo credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images By  Michael Menzies Oct 31, 2026, 09:00 EDT Updated: Oct 30, 2026, 20:28 EDT Comments Add to Preferred Sources The Edmonton Oilers begin a quick East Coast road trip with a Halloween matinee against the New York Islanders .  Their start has been the opposite of the Amityville Horror, being the last undefeated road team in the NHL (5-0-0) heading into this three-game stretch in four days.  Withstanding some crucial injuries to get to a 9-2-2 record, the Oilers’ schedule becomes awfully compact: with seven games in a total of 12 days, and 13 games in the next 23 days.  She gets busy, and nine of those 13 games are on the road.  “I say to you guys every day, we want to win today,” said head coach Mike Babcock after practice on Friday. “You might as well embrace what’s going on in your life and then get the best out of that possible thing.” But what’s helped is the lack of grey area in their game. Trent Frederic has talked about this before, as well, and Mattias Ekholm mentioned it specifically after practice on Friday.  Babcock is laying out exactly what they need to do and what he wants.  “There will always be some, but I think they’re very few,” said Ekholm. “You have to work on instinct, you got to be able to try to take away that buffer time of understanding what’s happening and just reacting and make sure the other guys react to you.” Depth ying and yang
 A welcome sight for Oilers fans on Wednesday was seeing other names populate the box score. Although everyone is enjoying Connor McDavid’s historic run to begin the season, the anxieties about the bottom-six’s contributions (lack thereof) are palpable in Oil Country.  Mathieu Joseph scored his third goal, and Kasperi Kapanen fired home on his fourth, as Kapanen was put back on the top power play unit with Zach Hyman’s absence.  Both are tied with fifth in team scoring with six points, a far cry from McDavid, who is blowing away the rest of the league at 36 points.  On the flip side is Jake Walman, who skated as the team’s seventh defenceman again.  Babcock said he would be meeting with Walman again on Friday, and gave a similar speech to the media that he gave regarding Isaac Howard a week or so ago.  “What you’re going to do is you’re going to put your work boots on, and you’re going to get back to work, and you’re going to feel good about working hard that day,” said Babcock.   “Then when you get prepared for your opportunity, when you get it, you’re normally ready. When you feel bad, when you don’t put in the work, you feel sorry for yourself. When you get the opportunity, you’re not ready.  “Now, I’m not trying to pretend life is fair, but I’m gonna say to you, embrace whatever you’ve been given and make it better.”  This goes back to the lack of grey area and accountability that the Oilers’ leaders wanted in bringing in Babcock.  “You’re getting called out on whatever you’re not doing right to help the team win,” said Leon Draisaitl. “We’ve asked for that, we need that, we wanted that, and we’re getting it. That’s a good thing.  “I think we all understand within our group that no one is allowed to do anything more than anyone else, right? Yes, of course, your top-end guys, they might have a little bit of a longer leash when it comes to offence.  “But at the end of the day, our identity and the way we play, we’re all going to play the same way, and we’re all going to have the same mindset towards that. He’s very hard on that, and that’s the way we want it and the way it should be.”  It’s Shaefer’s world, and we’re living in it
 Matthew Schaefer is taking over the world.  At least, he’s taken the NHL by storm. The reigning Calder Trophy winner just turned 19 in September, and played the overtime hero again on Thursday night, as the New York Islanders defeated the Minnesota 4-3.  It was Schaefer’s second goal of the game, extending his point streak to six games, and completed back-to-back contests topping 30 minutes of ice time. On Tuesday, the wunderkind became the first player since tracking began to play all five minutes of overtime.  Absurd stuff.  “I was happy to get that one there,” Schaefer said about his 2-on-1 goal to finish the Wild.  As modest as he is, Schaefer is performing as well as any teenage defenceman ever has in league history, helping the Isles got off to this 7-4-2 start, and only suffering one regulation loss in their last six.  Schaefer may have been the piece that lured Pete DoBoer back into coaching. The Isles stunned the hockey world at the end of last season, firing Patrick Roy with just four games left to go, seeing if they couldn’t jumpstart a late push to make the playoffs.  DeBoer has accumulated many wins in his NHL career, 670 in fact, and would’ve had his pick of the litter in the off-season for coaching jobs. He hopped on the opportunity in Long Island.  “Gutsy effort by our group,” DeBoer said after the Minny game. “I thought we played a real complete game. Didn’t beat ourselves. We put the puck in good places. Both special teams were good. That’s a formula to give yourself a chance to win in a tough road building.” This is an awkward scheduling spot for the Isles. They just wrapped up a three-game homestand and have this home game, but don’t play again after until Thursday.  Notes:
 When I looked at Iyla Sorokin’s numbers vs. the Oilers, I was surprised he was only 4-3-2 vs. EDM. It seems like he’s always stealing games, as he did in his last matchup on Jan. 15 where he posted a ridiculous 35-save shutout (which isn’t his most impressive shutout vs EDM). However, Edmonton hasn’t beaten him in regulation since Nov. 13, 2023 (2-0-2). Only once has he faced fewer than 30 shots. 
 This is all happening without arguably New York’s best offensive player. Matt Barzal hasn’t played a game yet this season with a knee injury. He had good health a season ago, playing 81 games, and producing 72 points, the third-highest total of his career.  
 Bo Horvat has points in five of last six games, totalling 14 overall.  
 Quickly on Schaefer, here are some things he’s done this week.  Became the seventh defenseman in League history to record at least 70 points (25 goals, 45 assists) as a teenager . Surpassed Bobby Orr for 2nd most goals as teenage defencemen. Became first teenage defenseman in NHL history with three career overtime goals. Schaefer’s five career multigoal games tied Phil Housley for the most by a teenage defenseman in NHL history.  
 Connor McDavid set another NHL record with the longest assist streak to begin a season with 13 games. However, Leon Draisaitl’s point streak was snapped at seven games.  
 McDavid registered his second career 25-assist month (also 25 in February 2024). McDavid is the third player in NHL history to accomplish the feat multiple times. Gretzky did it 14 times and Mario Lemieux three times. 
 Wednesday was also just McDavid’s second game this year under 20 minutes of ice-time. He is averaging 23:30 a night.
 Babcock confirmed Tristan Jarry as the starter, and has been coy about whether Matt Tomkins would play on this road trip.
 Ekholm’s goal was the 11th by an Oilers defenseman this season, which as of Wednesday night, tied the Utah Mammoth for most in the NHL. 
 Oilers struggled vs the Eastern Conference last year going 13-16-3. However, they were 8-7-1 on the road. Interesting, that record was flipped in 2024-25, going 16-13-3. 
 EDM has a 5-4-1 in their last 10 vs the NYI.
 Michael Menzies is an Oilersnation columnist and co-host of Pregaming and Postgaming. He’s also been the play-by-play voice of the Bonnyville Pontiacs in the AJHL since 2019.
